correctness.rationale: The sum-system/bounded proper-color factorization bijection is independently checked against Huxley–Lettington–Schmidt (2026), eqs. (5.1)-(5.2), and direct word enumeration. The rational generating function has difference-coordinate residue B=m/(m-1)^2. Marking all restricted primes gives T(s,u)=Z_S(s) product_p (1-u_p p^{-s})^{-1}-1, so fixed vector extraction has the computed strictly positive pole order E+1 with multinomial coefficient E!/product(e_p!). Boundary uniqueness follows from two multiplicatively independent primes outside finite S; the exact Hwang–Janson Section 2 statement of Delange applies to nonnegative coefficients, yielding the constant divided by rho Gamma(E+1). An unrestricted simple-pole calculation proves rho_S<r_m and joint valuation escape. Python 3 standard-library verify.py ran with VERIFY_OK for m=2..4,n<=112 including simultaneous 2-/3-valuation slices; finite checks supplement the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The cited 2026 Theorem 5.3 gives an unrestricted Dirichlet series, whereas the claimed all-finite-S, all-fixed-exponent-vector asymptotic specifies a smaller growth exponent, exact logarithmic degree E, and a nontrivial product constant. Law–Lettington–Schmidt (2025) gives fixed-size factorization enumeration, not the local summatory law. Hwang–Janson (2009) provides Delange methods and covers a simpler 2-part zero-valuation special case via allowed-factor subsets; its inspected results do not give the vector-specific asymptotic. Public searches and published-index comparisons located no implication-equivalent stronger coverage. General weighted-factorization methods could imply the result indirectly; uncertainty is documented.
residual_risks: A broad weighted-order-factorization theorem could contain this fixed-vector case implicitly; searched/inspected results did not demonstrate that implication.
The 2026 preprint references a submitted 2026 companion on c-polynomial factorizations whose full content was not independently inspected.
The 2019 foundational sum-systems paper was checked only through its abstract; priority based on its full text remains a limited-access risk.

value.rationale: Arithmetic valuation strata give a canonical local filtration of the already-motivated global sum-system counting function. For every finite S and every fixed nonnegative exponent vector, the result computes an exact natural leading asymptotic and its root rho_S, with the logarithmic degree E determined by total forced prime multiplicity. As a meaningful probabilistic consequence, prime exponents in the system size escape any fixed bound jointly. This is a nontrivial structural family with plausible use in refined random-sum-system statistics; not a finite exercise or arbitrary slice.
